questions.q: Why does Wong say traveling abroad is so valuable?
a: It forces self-reliance and shows you life beyond your local bubble
It guarantees a better job when you return home
It lets you escape your family's expectations permanently
It teaches you to avoid unfamiliar cultures and customs
questions.why: Lesson 1 says time abroad builds independence and exposes you to a wider reality.

questions.q: What effect did Haunani-Kay Trask's talk have on Wong?
a: It inspired her to travel further and carry herself with confidence
It convinced her to give up comedy and study Hawaiian history
It made her decide to stay close to home after college
It taught her to hide her background from classmates
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Trask's confidence and pride as the spark for Wong's bigger travels.

questions.q: What does Wong advise about race and gender labels?
a: Look past them and concentrate on what you contribute
Use them to explain away any criticism you receive
Let them determine which careers are open to you
Avoid discussing them with anyone at work
questions.why: Lesson 2 says her value comes from her sets, not her clothes or skin color.

questions.q: What did Wong do after learning a crush did not like her back?
a: She stopped wasting time on him and moved on
She gave up her plans to study in Vietnam
She complained about him to her professors
She changed her entire sense of humor to impress him
questions.why: Lesson 1 recounts that she remembered Trask's talk and refused to wallow in self-pity.

questions.q: Whose sacrifices does Wong remember when she feels like complaining?
a: Her grandfather's, who arrived alone in the US at eight
Her college roommate's, who supported her comedy career
Her comedy mentor's, who taught her to write jokes
Her daughter's, who inspired her Netflix specials
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes her grandfather sleeping on newspaper and the courage his story gave her.
